sources.title: Inherited authored SF Polo Fields water scenario
sources.locator: scenario.json: inputs and stages; results.json: operation
sources.use_and_limits: Our own teaching scenario, not a development application. The energy packet inherits its area, average IT demand, cooling concept, water factor and schedule. Frozen copies allow offline reproduction.

sources.title: Microsoft SJ04 fourth revised project description, July 2025
sources.locator: Printed pp.7–9 / PDF pp.8–10 cooling and PUE; printed p.20 / PDF p.21 water; printed p.13 / PDF p.14 electrical supply
sources.use_and_limits: Developer design estimate: average PUE 1.20 and peak 1.27. We transfer 1.20 as an authored annual electrical energy ratio, not measured Polo performance. Original load/design weather assumptions differ. Source includes hybrid closed-circuit evaporative cooling; actual SF fit and service are unassessed. Do not transfer its capacity, peak PUE, substation or recycled-water connection.

sources.title: EPA ENERGY STAR technical reference for data centers, August 2018
sources.locator: Printed p.9 / PDF p.9, example calculation
sources.use_and_limits: Distinguishes site and source energy. Its mixed-fuel source-energy scoring example is not the chosen site-electricity PUE model. No ENERGY STAR score is calculated.

sources.title: LBNL 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
sources.use_and_limits: Cooling, climate, setpoints and operation affect PUE and water performance. National simulations do not supply a matched pair of validated Polo cooling designs. No national forecast or water-consumption factor is transferred.

sources.title: SFPUC Hetch Hetchy Power for Developers
sources.locator: Eligibility; How It Works; Hetch Hetchy Power Service Points and PG&E Distribution Grid
sources.use_and_limits: City-owned-property development is required to apply; SFPUC evaluates service options and infrastructure. Describes service points involving PG&E distribution. Application is not confirmed service or spare capacity for this fictional campus. Replaces an older URL that now returns 404.

sources.title: SFPUC CleanPowerSF frequently asked questions
sources.use_and_limits: CleanPowerSF procures electricity while PG&E delivers and maintains lines for its customers. Regional example explaining procurement versus delivery; do not assign this programme or a feeder to the campus.

sources.title: California ISO large loads
sources.locator: Interconnection studies and cost recovery; technical requirements
sources.use_and_limits: Local utility tariffs govern retail-load interconnection; CAISO accounts for large loads in broader planning. Does not establish Polo spare capacity, upgrade size, lead time or household outages.

sources.title: California Energy Commission summer reliability
sources.locator: Opening explanation of temperature and air-conditioning demand
sources.use_and_limits: Supports shared regional hot-weather demand context. No numerical Polo heatwave or drought multiplier and no shortage prediction.

sources.title: Caterpillar 320D3 GC features and benefits
sources.locator: PDF p.1 fuel use; p.4 engine notes
sources.use_and_limits: Manufacturer earthmoving example states typical 11–13 L/hour; midpoint 12 is an illustrative grading-rate anchor. The brochure describes a noncertified-emission engine. This is not a machine procurement proposal, California-compliance claim or validated Polo fuel rate. Other machinery rates remain wholly authored.

sources.title: LBNL United States Data Center Energy Usage Report 2025 Update landing page
sources.use_and_limits: Current report overview checked; national forecasts are not inputs. Full report was not obtained, so its detailed numerical parameters are not used.
